page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-400s-amd is a dedicated-thread virtual machine within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, configured with 1 physical core presenting 2 dedicated vCPUs via multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 16 GB, resulting in an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8 GB per vCPU). The host configuration includes 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per core. Local storage is directly integrated as a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. The server does not contain a discrete GPU.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a notable divergence between single-threaded efficiency and parallel aggregate throughput. Single-core evaluations place the instance in the upper 25th percentile, supported by a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and a stress-ng single-core output of 2934.07. Text processing operations also register strong throughput. However, overall multi-core compute marks—including Geekbench multi-core (3785.0), PassMark CPU (5470.65), and Clang compilation (4376.0)—remain in the lower quartile due to the two-thread constraint. Uncached memory bandwidth tests show average capabilities (74.28 GB/s read, 53.91 GB/s write), while static web serving throughput (2.26 GB/sec) and PassMark database metrics reflect the bounded concurrency of the underlying single physical core.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the instance balances a generous 16 GB memory pool and 400 GB of high-speed NVMe storage against a lean dual-vCPU footprint. This eliminates the necessity of purchasing detached block storage for medium-sized working sets while keeping computing resource overhead contained. The configuration is optimal for memory-focused services that do not require high parallel concurrency, such as dedicated in-memory caches, staging database instances, continuous integration runners, lightweight ETL pipelines, and internal backend services.
description: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor platform, running at 2.0 GHz. The server provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 16 GB of system memory and 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware benchmarks reflect a distinct performance profile: single-threaded execution is strong, as demonstrated by Geekbench and stress-ng single-core results in the top quartile, alongside high text-processing throughput. Conversely, overall multi-core performance, static web serving throughput, and database operational benchmarks place in lower percentiles due to the two-thread ceiling. With an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, the instance delivers efficient memory density and integrated high-capacity solid-state storage without requiring supplementary block storage attachments. This configuration is well aligned with memory-heavy background tasks, caching tiers, lightweight data pipelines, and staging database instances.
